newsitem.title: USA: US Airways may be forced to downsize despite profit.
newsitem.headline: US Airways may be forced to downsize despite profit.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc. said Wednesday it returned to profitability in the first quarter, but added that it suffered losses in key markets and needed to cut costs to remain competitive.

The company has been struggling to reach a labour agreement with its pilots and has raised the possibility that it could reduce the size of the airline to remain competitive if no agreement is reached.
The carrier's announcement sent its shares soaring $4.625, or 16 percent, to $33.50 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most actively traded issues.

The airline, formerly called USAir, said it posted a record profit of $152.7 million for the three months ended March 31 on revenues of $2.1 billion. That compared with a loss of $32.3 million on revenues of $1.9 billion in the first quarter of 1996.

The company added that, after allowing for a $20.9 million preferred dividend requirement, the net profit applicable to common shareholders was $131.8 million, or $2 a share. That compared with 1996 loss of $54.6 million, or 86 cents a share.

While the group's earnings easily topped Wall Street expectations of 69 cents a share, the airline said it continued to experience "significant losses in key markets as a result of an uncompetitive cost structure and the escalating incursion of low-cost carriers."

It added that discussions to reduce costs "have now gone on for many years without progress." This lack of progress, it said, "leaves us no choice but to conclude that the company must promptly implement the appropriate steps to address the issue."
One possible step would be reducing the size of the airline, which has one of the highest cost structures in the industry.
In meetings with employees over the past two weeks, US Airways management outlined two possibilities -- getting a competitive cost structure in place or downsizing the airline.

"The preferred path, based on achieving a competitive cost structure, leads to US Airways's growth into a major international competitor. The other path leads to the company becoming a smaller, regional carrier with a continued focus on quality," the company said Wednesday.
The airline did not provide details on its possible plans.
US Airways has been in protracted labour talks with its pilots union. Although the two sides continue to meet, progress on the contract negotitiations has been slow.
The airline said its first quarter results benefited from favourable economic and weather conditions, as well as the performance of the carrier's 42,000 employees.
